name: quadrupole-rf
description: A mass filter: four round rods driven by an RF supply, with the x pair and the y pair in antiphase. The same rods as the static quadrupole template, but operated rather than merely charged - which makes it the device where the field solve and the time-domain integrator have to be right together. The two pairs are exact negatives of one another, so the whole structure reduces to a single basis solve whose weight is a function of time; nothing is re-solved as the drive swings. Expect the stability boundary to sit close to the ideal hyperbolic one but not on it: round rods carry a 12-pole component that a hyperbola does not, and the boundary moves with it. Setting the DC to zero puts the working point on the a = 0 line, where the low-mass cut-off is the single number to compare against.

inscribedRadius.description: Axis to nearest rod surface, conventionally r0. Everything scales with it: the Mathieu q goes as r0 squared at fixed voltage.

rodRatio.description: Rod radius as a multiple of the inscribed radius. 1.1468 cancels the leading non-ideal multipole, the 12-pole; move away from it and the stability boundary moves too, which is the effect this template exists to make measurable.

rfAmplitude.description: Zero to peak, applied to the x pair; the y pair takes its negative. Sets the Mathieu q, which is 4 z e V / (m omega^2 r0^2).

dcPotential.description: Applied to the x pair as a steady offset; the y pair takes its negative. Sets the Mathieu a, which is 8 z e U / (m omega^2 r0^2). Zero puts the working point on the a = 0 line, where the filter passes everything above the low-mass cut-off.

driveFrequency.description: One generator for the whole structure. Raising it lowers q at fixed voltage, so frequency and amplitude trade against each other at a fixed working point.

waveformDutyCycle.description: Only meaningful for a rectangular drive, which this template does not select by default. Away from one half the wave carries a mean that acts as a DC offset - the trick of a digital mass filter.

housingClearance.description: Rod centre to the grounded wall, beyond the rod radius, as a multiple of the rod radius. The classical rod ratio assumes no housing, so this says how far a given design sits from that assumption.

cellsPerRadius.description: Grid cells across the inscribed radius. The rod surfaces are cut cells, so the boundary is resolved below one cell, but the multipole content still converges with the mesh.

launchOffset.description: How far off axis the ion starts, in both transverse directions. Small enough to be a probe of stability rather than a test of acceptance.

ionEnergy.description: Axial energy carrying the ion through. It does not enter the stability condition at all - the transverse motion is governed by a and q alone - so it sets how many RF cycles the ion spends inside and nothing else.
